messages:
marie: Heads up — need a quick RICE recalibration for the upcoming quarter. Two customer-driven asks popped to the top: (A) per-tenant routing SLA bump for enterprise customers, (B) granular quota + explainability for billing/sales demos. Need sequencing decision this week.
sam: Can we quantify impact vs engineering risk? SLA change touches runtime, cache, and routing. That could be noisy.
deepa: From ops POV: SLA bump for top 3 customers is high-touch but limited surface area in the control plane. Rough effort: infra + validation ~3 sprints if we do a full rollout. Canary could reduce risk.
ethan: Data point: ARR at risk if we don't deliver SLA bump for those 3 = ~$350k over 12 months (churn/discount risk). Not sure how to fold ARR into standard RICE — should it be a multiplier?
marie: Proposal: keep RICE but allow an "ARR multiplier" clipped to max 3x to reflect commercial stakes. So impact_score = base_impact * min(3, customer_arr/100k). This prevents a single customer from hijacking the board but still acknowledges revenue. Thoughts?
jess: Design: quota explainability is small surface — we can do a minimal UI and help text MVP in ~1 sprint. High perceived value for demos.
rebecca: Sales confirms: quota explainability directly unblocks two active deals this quarter (~$100k ARR/mo potential). Strong ask.
sam: Engineering realism: SLA bump risk = perf regressions + testing surface. Canary + fallback needed. If we count canary + infra + runtime changes it's effort ~6 person-months.
marie: Let's do a quick RICE calc with our current heuristics (Reach=customers impacted this quarter, Impact 1-10, Confidence % as usual, Effort in person-months).
marie: ```
Feature | Reach | Impact | Confidence | Effort(pm) | RICE
SLA bump | 3 | 8 | 60% | 6 | (3*8*0.6)/6 = 2.4
Quota explain | 10 | 6 | 80% | 2 | (10*6*0.8)/2 = 24
```
marie: Baseline says quota explain wins by a lot. If we plug in ARR multiplier for SLA bump: (3*8*0.6*3)/6 = 7.2 — still below quota explain but not negligible.
deepa: +1 for sequencing: ship quota explain first to hit demos, start canary work for SLA bump in parallel (part-time) to reduce total calendar time.
ethan: Agree with hybrid: shipping quota explain reduces short-term GTM risk; starting canary early reduces blast radius and smooths infra work.
sam: OK engineering plan: 2-week MLP for quota explain (PM + design + 1 eng). SLA bump: canary checklist + infra prep (2 wks part-time) then focused 4-wk sprint to finish. I'll write the canary checklist and fallout plan.
marie: Decision: move quota explain to MLP for next sprint. SLA bump scoped as follow-on with canary prep starting now. We'll apply ARR multiplier in the RICE sheet for enterprise asks but cap at 3x. @rebecca please surface which customers to notify.
rebecca: Will notify top 3 customers and tie expectations to the canary timeline.
jess: I'll drop MLP wires by EOD and iterate with Sam.
sam: On it — checklist + minimal fallback plan by EOD.
marie: I'll update the roadmap doc and the canonical RICE sheet with the ARR multiplier notes + sequencing decision.
prio-bot: roadmaps/redwood: roadmap doc updated: feature "quota explainability" moved to Sprint N, "SLA bump" scheduled for Sprint N+1 (canary prep started).
marie: Thanks all. We'll reconvene after canary checklist to confirm final effort and confidence numbers. :thumbsup:
